STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE SOP-26117
Pervaporation Membrane Test Rig - Safe Operating Limits
Rev 3, Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (Training Document)

1. PURPOSE
This SOP defines the safe operating envelope of the laboratory pervaporation
rig used for solvent dehydration studies with polymeric membranes.

2. OPERATING LIMITS
- Maximum allowable feed pressure: 4.0 bar(g). The feed pump discharge
  relief valve is set at 4.5 bar(g) and must never be blocked in.
- Normal feed pressure during a run: 2.0 to 3.0 bar(g).
- Feed temperature must stay between 40 and 70 degC. Membrane dama

Normal feed pressure during a run: 2.0 to 3.0 bar(g).
- Feed temperature must stay between 40 and 70 degC. Membrane damage is
  likely above 75 degC.
- Permeate side vacuum must remain below 20 mbar absolute. If vacuum
  exceeds 40 mbar for more than 60 seconds, shut down and check for leaks.
- Cooling water flow to the condenser must be verified before starting
  the vacuum pump.

3. STARTUP SEQUENCE
a) Verify drain valves are closed and impingers are seated in the cold trap.
b) Start cooling water and confirm flow at the sight glass.
c) Start the feed pump and set recirculation until feed te

.
b) Start cooling water and confirm flow at the sight glass.
c) Start the feed pump and set recirculation until feed temperature
   stabilises within the allowed band.
d) Start the vacuum pump slowly while watching the manometer.
e) Open the permeate valves to the left and right impingers alternately
   to collect condensate samples every 30 minutes.

4. SAMPLING AND ANALYSIS
- Permeate samples are taken from the sample port downstream of the cold
  trap and analysed for water content by Karl Fischer titration.
- Record feed pressure, feed temperature, permeate vacuum and flux every
  30 minu

er content by Karl Fischer titration.
- Record feed pressure, feed temperature, permeate vacuum and flux every
  30 minutes in the run log.

5. SHUTDOWN AND EMERGENCIES
- On power failure the vacuum break valve opens automatically to protect
  the membrane from oil back-migration.
- Any sudden flux drop with stable vacuum indicates membrane fouling;
  stop the run and replace the membrane sheet.
- Waste solvent is collected in the waste bucket and disposed of per
  hazardous waste procedure HAZ-04.
